title: State is a snapshot for that render

slides.say: This button calls set number three times. Click it, and the number only goes up by one. Why?
During this render, number is zero. So each line really says: set number to zero plus one. Three times, the same value.

slides.text: Setting state only changes it for the next render. Inside this render, number stays the same.
slides.say: Setting state does not change the variable you already have. It asks React for a new render, with the new value.
Even later, inside a timer, the alert shows zero. The handler was created with the snapshot from that render.

slides.text: A state variable never changes within a render, even in async code.
slides.say: The takeaway: each render has its own state values, and its own event handlers that see them.
